title.en: Anishinaabe Stories of Culture and Respect

paragraph.text_eng: OK, thank you. So let’s see this thing.

sentence.sent_text: Ahaw sa diibaajimon ahaw miigwech.
Aaniishinaa awe aya’aaaa.

paragraph.text_eng: I was given tobacco to talk about something and analyze a few things, the things that I was taught as I was growing up, especially this. So as we gather and sit around somewhere we all have different, our own, teachings, I would never say I disbelieve anyone.

sentence.sent_text: Asemaa ingii-miinigoo ji-naanaagazoondamaan gegoo ji-didibaadandamaan bangii awe, minik ge niin gegoo gaapi-izhi-waawiindamaagowaan gii-pi-ombigiyaan aapiji go awe.
Nashke ingoji gii-okwabiyang omaa ingoji gakina gakina bebakaan gidayaamin dibaajmowinan.
Gaawiin dash wiin awiya wiikaa indaa-aanwetawaasii aaniishnaa.

paragraph.text_eng: Everyone, everyone has something that they were taught as they grew up as a child; that is why I say this; I would never think to myself that person is not right. The truth, he speaks the truth; what he says, everyone speaks the truth. The things that he speaks about, such as here that which I was taught.

sentence.sent_text: Gakina, gakina awiiya gegoo gii-pi-waawiindamowaa gii-pi-abinoojiiwid mii dash iye gaa-onji-ikidowaan gawiin, gaawiin wiikaa awiiya anishaa ikido indaa-inendanzii.
Debwe, debwe iwe gaa-ikidod, gakina awiya debwe.
Minik gego gaa-izhi-dibaajimot awe, nashke omaa geniin gaa-izhi-gikinoo’amaagowaan.

paragraph.text_eng: Before you start something that you are going to do, first thing you do is pick up your tobacco, It is this, this is the one that will help you to do it right, whatever you are doing, anything you want to do.

sentence.sent_text: Jibwaa maajitaayan gegoo owe wii-izhichigeyan, akawe sa gidasemaa gidoodaapinaa.
Mii-dash awe, ge-wiiji’ik awe weweni gego ji-izhichigeyan aaniin, aaniin iwe gwek waa-izhichigeyan.

paragraph.text_eng: Whenever someone gets their game, such as a deer, It is here when you get your deer, you gut it right here and now. As you look inside the stomach, you know what you are looking for inside the stomach. The first thing to do, to work on, that is the one you should hang up, around clean ground. I can’t recall the name of it. It is among the stomach part there; it is attached just like, it looks like liver but it is smaller maybe four to six inches in diameter.

sentence.sent_text: Dibishko gonaa awiiya gii-nitaaget, nashke awe waawaashkeshi gii-ikodong.
Howa mii-sa imaa gii-nisat waawaashkeshi, mii-go omaa wewiib ezhi ezhi-bagojiinad.
In-aabiyan imaa biinji-misad, aaniishinaa gigikendaan omaa awegonen omaa biinjaya’ii nitam ge-ayaayan.
Ge-dazhiikaman, gii-agoodooyan sa go imaa, biinkamigaang.
Amanji ezhinikaadegwen eya’i.

Jiigi-misad igo omaa aasa-misad omaa izhi-izhi-agood izhi-ayaa, izhi-agogin-ini indigo eyii, indigo gegaa go okon izhinaagwad agaasin idash maagizhaa maagizhaa niiyo-mininj ingodwaaso-mininj izhi, izhi-waawiyeyaa.

paragraph.text_eng: This is why you gut it; first of all that is the one you cut off. And then you, you hang it up on a branch as high as the deer stands. That is how high you hang it. Then you put your tobacco down.

sentence.sent_text: Mii-dash iye gii-pagojiinad waawaashkeshi mii-awe bekwajizhaman.
Waa mii-sa ezhi, ezhi-agoodooyan imaa mitigoonsing ginaabaakogoodoon epiiji-gaabawid igo waawaashkeshi.
Mii epiit-agoodooyan.
Oo gidasemaa gibagidinaa.

paragraph.text_eng: “Thanks for this food that will carry me through, that I will feed my relatives and my children.”

sentence.sent_text: “Ohoo miigwech sa gii-miizhiyan owe ge-onji-waawiisiniyaan, ge-noonji-ashamagwaa ogowe indinawemaaganag niijaanisag.”

paragraph.text_eng: That is the thanks you give that allows you to have this deer.

sentence.sent_text: Mii-iwe ezhi-miigwechiwiyad awe gaa-inenimik ji-debinat aw waawaashkeshi.

paragraph.text_eng: Some other people I see them, and I hear them too. They are taught a little differently.

sentence.sent_text: Aanind awiiya niwaabamaag ninoondawaag sago gaye.
Bakaan ge-wiinawaa gegoo izhi-gikinoo’amawaawag.

paragraph.text_eng: Such as I worked with there at the time, when we were skinning the deer.

sentence.sent_text: Booshke awedi bezhig ingii-wiidanokiimaaban imaa gii, gii-bakonagit a waawaas-hkeshki.

paragraph.text_eng: As we were talking, we were explaining to the students that were watching us. “This is what I hang up,” I told them. And so he says, my partner, “This is what we do,” he said. So he cuts a little piece of the liver. “This is what we use,” he said.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash iwe indazhindaamin niwiindamowaanaanik sa go ogowe abinoojiiyag gaa ganawaabiyaat, “mii-awe egoodoowaan” indinaak.
Wah gewiin imaan, awe gaa-Wiiji’it “owe niinawind” ikido.
Ezhi-ayaa-aat ezhi-bakwezhang bangii eyii okon.
“Mii-awe niinawind aabajitoowaang” ikido.

paragraph.text_eng: “Oh yes,” I say he is right, what he says.

sentence.sent_text: “Owaah geget” indinaa geget debwe awe gaa-ikidod gaawiin.

paragraph.text_eng: I would never say that he is wrong. He knows his own teachings and this is, this is why I say this, that everyone is right (in their own teachings).

sentence.sent_text: Gaawiin wiikaa indaa-inaasii owe anish anishaa gosha ji-ikidod.
Ogikendaan ge-wiin gaa-izhi-gikinoo’amaawind mii-dash iye, gaa-onji-ikidowaan gakina awiiya akina awiiya debwe minik omaa e.

paragraph.text_eng: When you live in your community that is how you pass on the teachings. They all have their own stories as to how they pass on their teachings.

sentence.sent_text: Endanakiiyan, mii omaa gegiin ezhi-gikinoo’amaageyan ingojiwang ingoji waasa.
Awiya bizindaman booshke ingoding gii-ikobiiyaat gichi-aya’aag gakina bebikaan ikidowag akina ge-wiinawaa ogikendaanaawaa wa’-izhi-gikinoo amaagewaat.

paragraph.text_eng: No, I would not dishonor anyone. Where you are from, where you live, where your mother is from, your grandmother, your grandfather, this is where you look. Those are your teachings, those ones that raised you, that is what I believe. When I listen to others, I don’t dishonor what they say; I would never say that to anyone. (I would never say)“that is not the way” to anyone: I was always told not to disbelieve them, I was told to listen carefully, listen to someone for he may say it differently. You will help him the way he does it. This is what I was told; I would never dishonor anyone.

sentence.sent_text: Gaawiin, kaawiin awiiya indaa-aanwetawaasii.
Wenjiiyan imaa endaayan gaa-izhi-ogiiyan gaa-izhi’iw, ookomisiyan omishoomisiyan mii ima ge mii-imaa ge-inaabiyan.
Mii-iwe gigikinoo’amaagowin, igiwe gaagii-pi-ombigi’ikwaa mii niin iko enen-damaan owe ge.
Awiiya gegoo gii-bazindawag gaawiin indaa-anwetawaasii, gaawiin shwiin igo ge wiikaa indaa-inaasii awiiya.
gaawiin shwiin inakeya’ii ji-inag aaniishinaa ingii-onji’igoo.
Weweni gegoo ji-bizindamaan ingii-igoo, bazindaw awiiya, ingoji bakaan gegoo gii-ikido.
Mii-go iye nakeya’ii ge-izhi-waawiiji’at.
Mii niin owe gaa-igoowaan, gaawiin wiikaa awiiya gegoo indaa-anwetawaasii.

paragraph.text_eng: I listen carefully; I listen carefully to the way they talk. I fully understand the Anishinaabe language or the Ojibwe language; I understand also when they speak. When we gather somewhere, especially those ones that work on the Anishinaabe way of life and the Anishinaabe language, we all should listen to them carefully. We should all believe them; we should never think that they are lying to us; for sure they are telling the truth those ones that are different when they say things differently; they are fibbing because they, they were told and they were brought up that way and also some of them use their dreams and visions when they teach.

sentence.sent_text: Wewenii weweni imbazindam, weweni imbazindawaa gaa-gaagiigidowaad.
Weweni ge ninisidotaan owe gii-anishinaabe-gaagiigidod awiya gemaa ge gii-ojibwemod niinisidotawaag ga gaa-gaagiigidowaad.
Nashke awe gii-ayaat gii-okwabing ingoji, aayapiji go ogowe gaa-dazhiikamowaad owe anishnaabe-gikinoo’amaadiwin Anishinaabemowin, gakina awiya gidaa-weweni-bizindawaanaanik.

Geget gidaa-debwetawaanaanik gaawiin gaawiin wiikaa awiya, ji-inendamang owe anishaa maawi-in ikido ji-inendamang geget igo debwewag ingiwe bakaan gegoo bakaan wiinawaa gegoo gii-ikidowaad, gaawinoon anishaa ikidosiiwag aanishinaa gii-izhi, gii-izhi-wiindamawaawag gii-izhi-ombigiwag booshk ge gaye ingoding bawaajiganan awiya odaabajitoonaawaan gegoo gii-dibaajimod.

paragraph.text_eng: This is why, listen carefully and do not dishonor what they said; honor his ways; he is truthful in what he is saying.

sentence.sent_text: Mii-dash iwe onji-dago, weweni ji-naanaagazodawad gego aanwedawaaken, debwetaw, geget gosha go debwe gaa-ikidod.

paragraph.text_eng: Thank you, okay that is it; thank you all for listening to me.

sentence.sent_text: Ahaw sa miigwech, ahaw mii-sa gonaa-e miigwech bazindawiyeg ahaw sa.

paragraph.text_eng: My fellow Anishinaabe has given me this tobacco to speak here, but I don’t know what it is that I should talk about, the Anishinaabe culture, and what was decided for him to do when he arrived here.

sentence.sent_text: Aw asemaa ingii-pi-miinig wa’aw niij-anishinaabe omaa da-gaagiigidoyaan, gaawiin-sh ingikendanziin awegodogwen ge-dazhindamowaanen omaa, o’ow igo Anishinaabe ezhitwaad miinawaa gaa-pi-inaakoniged inaakoniged ge mii omaa gii-tagoshing.

paragraph.text_eng: It is close to here, where I was raised, along the border of the place called Wisconsin. I was raised by those elders; they are the ones who taught me everything I remember a lot of what they told me, of this way the Anishinaabe does things.

sentence.sent_text: Mii omaa besho gaa-tazhi-nitaawigiyaan imaa jiigayi’ii imaa Wisconsin ezhi-wiinjigaadeg.
Ingii-nitaawig’igoog ingiw chi-aya’aag, mii ingiw akina gegoo gaa-waawiindamawijig.
Omaa minik igo nimikwendaan gaa-izhi-wiindamawiwaad, ow keyaa ezhichiged aw Anishinaabe.

paragraph.text_eng: See when I was growing up here, we always went to the dances when the big drums were being used. And also when there was Midewin I would go around with them, playing around there (in the camp area)of where it was going on. They always only spoke Ojibwe, and you see I too speak good Ojibwe as best as I can.

sentence.sent_text: Nashke gii-pi-nitaawigiyaan apane ingii-izhaamin iwidi niimi’idiwaad aabadiziwaad ingiw manidoo-dewe’iganag.
Miinawaa gaye ko gii-midewing ingii-paa-wiijiiwaag ingii-paa-wijii’aawaag imaa gii-paa-dazhitaayaan imaa endanakamigak jiigay’ii.
Meta go apane go gii-ojibwemowaad, nashke gaye niin ninitaa-ojibwem igo indiniwaaz.

paragraph.text_eng: That is how I came to know how to speak Ojibwe. I think it was later on, when I was seven years old that I began to speak English.

sentence.sent_text: Mii imaa gaa-onji-gikendamaan i’iw da-Ojibwemoyaan.
Baamaa wiin imaa apii ganabaj ingii-niizhwaaso-biboonigiz gii-maajii-Zhaaganaashiimoyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: I would always listen to the elders when they would be talking about something. See, they were elders; and all of the ones that would come visit them were some elders. Oo, they would speak when they visited one another; they would talk about everything, even what had happed long ago, and what was going on with them these days and what would be happening later. They talked about everything as I listened to them.

sentence.sent_text: Apane ko ingii-pizindawaag ingiw chi-aya’aag gegoo gii-tazhindamowaad.
Nashke gaye gii-chi-aya’aawiwag, miish iniw akina apane gaa-pi-mawidisigowaajin iniw chi-aya’aan aanind.
Oo, gii-kaagiigidowaad gii-mawadisidaadiwaad, akina gegoo ogii-tazhindaanaawaa akina gegoo wawaaj igo ge i iw gaa-izhiwebak mewinzha, miinawaa ezhiwebadining noongom miinawaa go waa-izhiwebak naagaj.
Akina gegoo ogii-tazhindaanaawaa gii-pabizindawagwaa.

paragraph.text_eng: Once and a while they would chase me outside, “Why don’t you go play around outside,” they said to me.

sentence.sent_text: Aaningodinong ko ge ingii-zaagijinaazha’ogoog, “Daga, agwajiing baa-dazhitaan” ingii-igoog.

paragraph.text_eng: “OK.” So outside by the window I would eavesdrop on what it was they were talking about.

sentence.sent_text: “Ahaw.” Miish imaa waasechiganing agwajiing mii imaa gaa-tazhi-giimoozitawagwaa ko wegonen endazhindamowaad.

paragraph.text_eng: And after I had grown up a bit more, while I was going to school, that’s when I heard the white man. Must have been a preacher who told of what will happen in the future; everyone will burn (in hell), everyone.

sentence.sent_text: Mii iw dash azhigwa gaa-ani-nitaawigiyaan igo nawaj, megwaa gii-kikinoo’amaagoziyaan, mii imaa azhigwa gii-noondawag aw chimookomaan gaagiigidod anama’e-winini iidog aw, ge-wiin dibaajimod waa-izhiwebadinig, akina ingoding wii-chaagizowag akina.

paragraph.text_eng: He scared me by saying that. After I got home I told those old people, the ones who raised me. “Hey, someday, supposedly we’re all going to burn in hell, everyone. Everyone of us is going to burn.”

sentence.sent_text: Mii imaa gaa-izhi-zegimid.
Gaa-kiiweyaan gaa-izhi-wiindamawagaa ingiw chi-aya’aag, gaa-nitaawigi’ijig, “He, ingoding giiwenh giwii-chaagizomin akina.
Mii go akina go ge-izhi-jaagizoyang.”

paragraph.text_eng: That old lady said, “Where the heck did you get that?”

sentence.sent_text: “Aaniin dana wendinaman iw?” ikido aw mindimooyenh.

paragraph.text_eng: “Aa that one white guy told me, he was speaking at the school; I think it was called’religious instructions.’ He scared me saying that.”

sentence.sent_text: “Aa ingii-wiindamaag aw bezhig chi-mookomaan gii-kaagiigido iwidi gikinoo’amaadiwagamigong, mii go iidog iw’religious instructions’ gaa-izhinikadeg.
Mii imaa gaa-izhi-zegimid.”

paragraph.text_eng: The that old lady told me, “Don’t believe him; that’s their way that they believe; their beliefs are in that big book that they read. That is not our way to believe; we are Anishinaabe. That’s why we always offer tobacco, and why we have our dances, and why we are Mide, everything. This is the way for us to believe.”

sentence.sent_text: Gaa-izhi-wiindamawid aw mindimooyenh, “Gego debwetawaaken a’aw.
Mii wiin akeyaa ezhi-debwetamowaad iw, ezhi-debwendamowaad iw chi mazina’igan egindamowaad.
Gaawiin giinawind gidizhitwaasiimin iw gidanishinaabewimin giinawind.
Mii wenji-bagidinang apane aw asemaa, miinawaa wenji-nimii’idiiyang miinawaa ge wenji-midewiyang akina gegoo.
Mii giinawind ow akeyaa ezhitwaayang.”

paragraph.text_eng: “Oh.” I was still scared of what that white man had said.

sentence.sent_text: “Oo.” Booch idash igo ingii-segimig aw chi-mookomaan.

paragraph.text_eng: And then after I grew up, I just had to sneak into churches, so I could listen to more of the preachers.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash azhigwa gaa-nitaawigiyaan booch igo ko gaa-giimooji-biindegeyaan iniw anama’ewigamigoon, nawaj wii-pizindawagwaa ingiw gagiikwewininiwag.

paragraph.text_eng: And I approached those elders and asked them about everything too, listening to what they had to say. And then it was when I was about 32-years-old when I realized there is only one Creator.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa gegoo ingii-naazikawaag ko ingiw chi-aya’aag gagagwejimagwaa akina gegoo, bizindawagwaa ge eyikidowaad.
Mii dash iw gaa-maaminonendamaan ingoji gaa-nisimadana-ashi-niizho-biboonigiziyaan meta go bezhigod a Manidoo naagaanizid.

paragraph.text_eng: He put every single walk of life here on earth, the white people, black people, Asians, and Anishinaabe. And we were all spiritual, given a language to speak, and a spiritual way of life that we are to use when calling upon them, when calling upon the Creator.

sentence.sent_text: Bebakaan, bebakaan omaa akiing ogii-asaan iniw bemaadizinijin, ingiw chi-mookomaanan, makadewiiyaasag, aniibiishikewininiwag miinawaa Anishinaabeg.
Miinawaa ge gigii-miinigoowizimin i’iw akeyaa ge-inweyang, miinawaa ge-izhitwaayang ge-aabajitooyang ganoonangwaa ingiw, ganoonang aw manido.

paragraph.text_eng: This one is the language of ours, our language that will lead us into the future.

sentence.sent_text: Mii bezhig iw gidinwewininaan mii iw naagaaniimagak gidinwewininaan.

paragraph.text_eng: For almost 40 years I have been teaching the Ojibwe language, trying to help my fellow Anishinaabe seeking to speak the Ojibwe language, to carefully and properly call upon the manidoo when he offers tobacco. That is what I teach today, the reason I am teaching those students. There are many young people today who are pursuing our language. Indeed they are doing a good job. Indeed they are doing good as they pursue our culture.

sentence.sent_text: Ingoji go gegaa niimidana endaso-biboon ingikinoo’amaage iw Ojibwemowin gagwe-wiidookawag aw niij-anishinaabe nanda-nitaa-ojibwemod, weweni ge, weweni ge da-ganoonaad sa go iniw manidoon asemaan bagidinaad.
Mii gekinoo’amaageyaan noongom mii wenji-gikinoo’amaageyaan wenji-gikinoo’amawagwaa ingiw gikinoo’amaaganag.
Baataniinowag noongom ingiw oshki-aya’aag azhigwa beminizha’angig iw gidinwewininaan.
Mii go geget minochigewaad.
Geget minochigewag iw biminizha’amowaad i’iw gidizhitwaawininaan.

paragraph.text_eng: You see we have almost lost the Ojibwe language. Nobody spoke at length, and nobody pursued Ojibwe for very long. Nowadays on the other hand, in the past 5 or maybe past 10 years, they have started to try to speak Ojibwe. Indeed they are doing a good job.

sentence.sent_text: Nashke gepaa giwanitoomin iw ojibwemowin.
Ginwenzh gaawiin awiya gii-ojibwemosiin ginwenzh gaawiin awiya ogii-piminizha’anziin iw ojibwemowin.
Miish noongom azhigwa dash ingoji eko-naano-biboonagak gemaa gaye gegaa eko-midaaso-biboonagak, azhigwa maajitaawaad ingiw oshki-aya’aag wii-kagwe-ojibwemowaad.
Geget minochigewag.

paragraph.text_eng: They should pursue more of the ceremonies, and the various things we do as Anishinaabe, like when speaking for when they’re going to put tobacco down or a dish is set, or at the dance when they will speak, or maybe to receive the visions and dreams they are spiritually given to give names, they’ll know the way to say it. Also the funeral, that is extremely important. That is what they should pursue more of to know the way to do them.

sentence.sent_text: Iw dash nawaj ge-biminizha’amawaapan i’iw akeyaa asemaakeng, anooji akeyaa ezhichigeyang anishinaabewiyang nashke, da-gaagiigidowaad asemaa, wii-asaawaad maagizhaa onaaganan wii-atoowaad maagizhaa niimi’idiing da-gaagiigidowaad, maagizhaa ge nitaa-bawaajiged awiya miinigoowizid a’aw da-wiindaawasod maagizhaa go oga-gikendaan akeyaa ge-ni-ikidod.
Miinawa ge i’iw maajaa’iwewin, mii iw gechi-apiitendaagwak i’iw.
Mii imaa ge-ni-biminizha’amawaapan nawaj i’iw da-gikendamowaad iw akeyaa ge-izhichigewaad.

chapter.eng_title: That’s Why I Speak the Language

paragraph.text_eng: And now maybe you guys could understand I’m going to put it down in Anishinaabe. As I left today it was noon to arrive over here from Hermantown over there its called were I came from.

sentence.sent_text: Noongom dash maagizhaa idaa-nisidotaanaawaa nindaanoo-aniishinaabewisidoon o’.
Noongoom pi-maajaayaan gii-naawakwemagad imaa wii-pi-dagoshinaan owidi Hermantown izhinikaade ningii-pi-onjibaa.

paragraph.text_eng: And so I turned on that radio in my car, when I left there to come here. When I took off there, I was wanting to arrive at one’o clock. And there I listened to the radio from Fond du Lac. WGZS maybe it’s called, 89.1, they said. And so I listened there. and they asked for someone to speak there, to talk there they said, “What do ya think about the contemporary pop cultures influence on them modern Indians,” they asked. “Someone should call in,” call in I guess. And so as I listened there I really thought about it. Mmmm, I don’t know, as I listened to those people speaking. You know all the various opinions they had while they were talking. And so that’s what I thought, me alone I thought. Perhaps someone should know where they are coming from (their thoughts). If someone wants to come from the way the old time Indians thought, then that’s the way he/she should do things.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash iw ningii-baskanebidoon iw makakoons medwegamaan indoodaabaaning bi-maajaayaan bi-maajiibizweyaan imaa wii-tagoshinaan ingo-diba’iganek.
Mii dash imaa bizindamaan iw mmakakoons.
Mii dash imaa wenjibaamagak Nagaajiiwanaang WGZS ganabaj izhinikaade, 89.1 ikidowag.

Mii dash imaa bizindamaan mii dash imaa gagwedwewaad, da-giigidowaad awiiya, da-giigidowaad omaa, ikidowaad “what do ya think about the contemporary pop cultures influence on them modern Indian,” gagwedwewag.
“Da-bi-giigidod awiiya,” call in I guess.
Mii dash imaa bizindamaan chi-nanaagidawendamaan.
Amanj iidog, bizindawagwaa dash ingiw gayaagiigidojig.
You know all the various opinion ayaamowaad awiiya omaa gaagiigidowaad.
Mii dash iw gaa-inendamaan, niin gaa-inendamaan niin eta go.
Maagizhaa booch awiiya da-gikendang aaniindi wenjabaad.
Giishpin wii-onjibaad keyaa ingiw gete anisninaabebaniig keyaa, mii iw keyaa ge-izhichigepan.

paragraph.text_eng: The way that I always thought, in that place here when I was small, when I was little, when I came along in time with those old elders, the ones who taught me to know how to speak the Ojibwe language well. And maybe I am not completely able to speak the language well. There was a lot they gave me for safe keeping for others, and every day, all day we were spoken to only in the Ojibwe language, all the time. And whenever we went someplace, we went out to visit, to see the Anishinaabeg, they only spoke the Anishinaabe language. And there near Minisinaakwaang every one of those Anishinaabeg still spoke the Anishinaabe language. And when I went over there, I went back over there a little north, Sandy Lake is the name of that Anishinaabe town. And over there, every Anishinaabe still spoke the Ojibwe language. They still understood the Anishinaabe language when someone spoke.

sentence.sent_text: Ke niin apane inendamaan, mii omaa gii-pi-agaashityeyaan, gii-pi-wiij-ayaawagwaa ingiw gichi ayaa’aag, niin ingiw gaa-gikinoo’amawijig da-nitaa-ojibwemoyaan.
Maagizhaa go gaawiin go da-wiinge-nitaa-ojibwemoyaambaan.
Niibowa dash ningii-niindaa’igoog mii go endaso-giizhik gabe-giizhik eta go ningii-ojibwemotaagoomin apane.
Miinawaa go ingoji gii-izhaayaang gii-o-mawadishiweyaang anishinaabeg gii-o-waabamangwaa mii eta go ay wiinawaa mii eta go apane gii-anishinaabemowaad.
Mii go maa besho maa Minisinaakwang kina ingiw Anishinaabeg geyaabi gii-anishinaabemowag.
Miinawaa iwidi izhaayaang bangii odi giiwe izhaayaang owidi bangii giiwedinong owidi Gaa-mitaawangaagaamaag izhinikaade iw anishinaabe oodenawens.
Mii gaye iwidi akina ingiw anishinaabeg geyaabi gii-ojibwemowag.
Geyaabi go gii-nisidotaanaawaa iw anishinaabemowin awiiya gaagiigidod.

paragraph.text_eng: And additionally there’s no one, maybe there’s someone, maybe this is why they won’t like me, maybe this is why, you know sometimes, sometimes people, you know, wonder about me. And nobody was Christian over there where we are from. Nobody. None of those Anishinaabeg went to church. And nobody was Christian. It’s only the Indian way. They used their tobacco. They went to the dance; they participated in Midewin. That’s the way they believed so they lived their life that way.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa go gaawiin awiiya, maagizhaa awiiya, ge-onji-zhiingenimigooyaan maybe this is why you know, sometimes, sometimes people, you know, wonder about me.
Miinawaa go gaawiin awiiya gii-anama’esiin iwidi keyaa niinawind wenjibaayaan.
Gaawiin awiiya.
Gaawiin awiiya ingiw anishinaabeg gii-izhaasiiwag anamayi’ewigamigong.
Gaawiin go gaye awilya gii-anamayesiin.
Mii eta go anishinaaben keyaa.
Gii-abaaji’aawaad asemaawaa.
Miinawaa go gii-izhaawaad niimii’idii miinawaa go gii-midewiwaa.
Mii eta go keyaa gaa-zhi-debwendamowaad gaa-izhitwaawaad sa go.

paragraph.text_eng: When I was small they were raising me, those old time Anishinaabeg, those elders, my grandfather and my grndmother, Ojiiganang, sometimes they referred to him as, Zay Zah. And my grandmother her name was Iikwez. My late grandfather, our father, we called him, we named him that, and bullhead was his clan. Bullhead is also my clan, after all, his son is my late father. My father’s name was Egawaate’ishkan. And I am also from the Bullhead clan. And so Ojiiganang, that’s the one he married, Iikwez, and her clan was Wolf. Wolf was that elder woman’s clan.

sentence.sent_text: Gii-pi-agaashiiyaan gii-pi-nitaawigi’iwaad ingiw gete-anishinaabebaniig, iniw gichi ayaa’aag, mishomisiban miinawaa nookomisiban, Ojiiganang, miinawaa go naanigodinong Ze Zaa gii-inaa.
Miinawaa dash igo okomisiban gii-izhinikaazod Iikwez.
Nimishomisiban, Dedenaan, niinawind ningii-inaanaan, ningii-izhinikaanaanaan miinawaa mii iniw awaasasii iniw odoodeman.
Mii iniw mii aw gaye niin nindoodem awaasasii aansh naa mii iniw ogosan oniijaanisan mii aw indedeyiban.
Egawaate’ishkan gii-izhinikaazon indedeyiban.
Mii dash iw gaye niin wenji-odoodemiiyaan aw awaasasii.
Mii dash aw Ojiiganang mii iniw gaa-wiidigemaad iniw Iikwez, mii dash gaye wiin iniw odoodeman, mii iw iniw ma’iingan.
Ma’iinganan ogii-doodemii aw mindimooye.

paragraph.text_eng: And so that’s the way I remember. As we went everywhere, even when it was Thanksgiving, they came and got us, they took us somewhere, to someone else’s house, when we were fed by them, On Thanksgiving Day. First someone there spoke when they lit their pipes, and carefully, as the smoke starts to take off, they sent their tobacco (to those spirits). That’s the way they practiced, those Anishinaabeg over there, where I am from. Maybe that’s why I speak the language. Maybe that’s why I can almost, in a good way, speak the Ojibwe language, why they think of me a certain way. I know how to speak the Anishinaabe language a little bit.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa go dash igo keyaa ezhi-mikwendamaan.
Akina goji gii-izhaayaan miinawaa go, gii-miigwechiwigiizhigak, gii-pinaanigooyaang, gii-izhiwinigooyaang ingoji awiiya bakaan endaad gii-ashamigooyaang, Miigwechiwigiizhigak.
Akawe awiiya imaa gii-kaagiigido ogii-zakawaawaan iniw odoopwaaganimiwaa weweni dash inimaadaabisod asemaa weweni gii-apagizindamawaawaad iniw.
Mii iw keyaa gaa-izhitwaawaad ingiw ansihinaabeg odi keyaa niin wenjibaayaan.
Mii iw, mii iw wenji-anishinaabemoyaan.
Weweni magizhaa go gegaa weweni wenji-nitaa-ojibwemoyaan, wenji-inenimigooyaan sa go nitaa-anishinaabemoyaan bangii.

paragraph.text_eng: And now as I am still talking about that time when I was little, there were still a lot of elders around. I could talk a lot about those old Indians that were there. The ones that I always communicated with, the way they practiced their life; they participated in Midewin; they were involved in that dance, when they always used their tobacco, those ones that way. The elders are always thought of highly by me. You see, after all, they carried with them the Anishinaabe way of doing things, beliefs. And we were the ones who received it. And that’s what was done to them, they were given the Indian way to take care of. And so, they in turn gave it to the next Indians, and suddenly, I was given something by them to take care of, the Indian way.

sentence.sent_text: Azhigwa dash igo geyaabi go iw apii debaadodamaan gii-pi-agaashiiyaan, geyaabi go gii-baatiniiniwag ingiw gichi-ayaa’aag.

Niibowa igo indaa-dibaadomaag ingiw geyaabi gaa-ayaajig owidi pane gaa-gaganoonagwaa mii iw keyaa gaa-izhitwaawaad keyaa gii-midewiwaad, gii-tazhiikamowaad iw sa niimii’idiing miinawaa go pane gii-ni-aabaja’aawaad iniw odasemaawaan ingiw keyaa.
Mii ingiw gichi-ayaa’aag mii ingiw apane gichi-apiitenimindwaa.
Aniish naa mii wiinawaa ogii-bimiwidoonaawaa iw sa anishinaabe izhichigewin, izhitwaawiwin.
Niinawind dash gi-ni-giimiinigoomin.
Mii iw gaye wiinawaa gaa-izhi’indwaa gaye wiinawaa gii-niindaa’aawag igo gaye wiinawaa iw sa anishinaabeg keyaa.
Mii dash igo gaye wiinawaa mii go naa aanike-miinaawaad iniw anishinaaben.
Mii dash igo imaa gaye niin gegapii imaa gaye niin gii-ondiziiyaan, gaye niin gii-niindaa’igooyaan iniw anishinaabe keyaa.

paragraph.text_eng: Sometimes they would ask us to go somewhere when I was small, and that’s when I went with those elders. I went over there. Whatever they were doing, they always spoke the Anishinaabe language to each other. And so that’s why I remember it. I didnt do anything great. Only at the same time, I was there at that time, in that Anishinaabe town. There at the time as it began there, when everything changed from the time when everyone knew the language, until that time. Everybody they only speak English now. Only a very little bit of the elders are still there. That’s it.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaash igo ingoji izhaayaan nindamigooyaang owidi gii-pi-agaashiiyaan, ningii-pi-wiijiiwaag ingiw gichi-ayaa’aag.
Mii owidi izhaayaan.
Mii awegodigwen izhichigewaad, mii iw pane go anishinaabemotaadiwaad.
Mii dash iw keyaa eta go wenji-mikwendamaan.
Gaawiin go niin go gegoo ningii-gichi-izhichigesiin.
Mii eta go maa naana’idaa ningii-ayaa iw apii maa anishinaabe-oodenaawensing.
Naanayidaa iw apii ningii-pi-nitaawigezh igo imaa apii azhigo imaa apii gii-ni-aanjiseg iw akina awiiya sa go gii-nisidotang iw anishinaabemowin biinish igo apii.
Gakina go sago eta go zhaaganaashiimowaad.
Gichi bangii eta go imaa geyaabi ayaawag gichi-ayaa’aag igo eta go geyaabi goo imaa eyaajig.
Mii iw.

paragraph.text_eng: Alright, I’m going to talk about another thing here. My little brother has asked me, “Why is our Ojibwe language, our Anishinaabe language so important?” Anishinaabe is who we are, indeed that is why today it is so important.

sentence.sent_text: Ahaw, miinawaa dash omaa noongom ninga-dazhindaan gegoo.
Niijikiwens ingii-kagwejimig, “Aaniish epiitendaagwak o’ow ojibwemowin, Anishinaabemowin?” Anishinaabe aawiyaang, geget sa omaa noongom mii wenji-apiitendaagwak o’ow.

paragraph.text_eng: At the time when the Creator first made Anishinaade, that is the time our language, it was accepted at that time. And also, the Anishinaabe always talked to each other. They always used the Ojibwe language, the Anishinaabe language.

sentence.sent_text: I’iwapii dash ya’aw naagaanizid gaa-ozhi’aad wayeshkad Anishinaabe, i’iwaapii gidinwewininaan, gaa-odaapinigaadeg i’iwaapii.
Miinawaa dash yao Anishinaabeg gii-ganoonidiwag.
Ojibwemowin, Anishinaabemowlm apane ogii-abajitoonaawaan.

paragraph.text_eng: At the time when the white man arrived here in Anishinaabe country, they built schools, and that is when the Anishinaabe children entered them. That is also when the white man said, “Don’t say that, dont speak Ojibwe.”

sentence.sent_text: I’iwaapii dash wayaabishkiiwejig gii-pi-dagoshinoog omaa Anishinaabewakiing.
Ozhigewag gikinoo’maadi-wigamigoon i’iwaapul dash gii-piindigewag Anshinaabensag.
I’iwaapii dash wayaabishkiwejig gii-ikidowaad, Gego ikidoken, gego aabajitooken o’o Ojibwemowin.”

paragraph.text_eng: And indeed at that time, if a child used your language, at that time the white man would fight the child. Indeed those white men were evil when they fought the kids. And indeed at that time some didn’t say it anymore, and still the Anishinaabe children don’t use the Ojibwe language.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa geget i’iwaapii dash giishpin weshki-aya’aad gii-aabajitood o’ow gidinwewin, iwaapii dash wayaabishkiiwed apii ogii-miigaanaawaan weshki-aya’aad.
Geget sa iwaapii maji-izhiwebiziwaad wiinawaa wayaabishkiwejig azhigwa dash gaa-izhi-miigaanaawaan weshki-aya’aag.
Mii sa geget i’iwaapii dash aanind gaawiin geyaabi gegoo gii-ikidosiin gaawiin geyaabi dash, Anishinaabensag ogii-aabajitoosiinaawaan o’ow Ojibwemowin.

paragraph.text_eng: And also later on after they left, they didn’t have them anymore there at school. And later at the time when their children were born, his children, then did not know our Ojibwe language. The children only knew English.

sentence.sent_text: Mii miinawaa dash baanimaa ishkwaa dash gii-maajaawag gaawiin keyaabe ayaawaasiiwag mii akeyaa imaa gikinoo’maadi-wigamigong.
Baanimaa apii dash azhigwa oniijaanisan gaa-izhi-ondaadiziwaad, gaawiin dash i iwaapii oniijaanisan ogikendanziinaawaan gidinwewininaan Ojibwemowin.
Mii eta go Zhaaganaashimowin ogikendanaawaan oshki-aya’aag.

paragraph.text_eng: Indeed the elders say our Ojibwe language is important. Yes and if at that time he wants to go in, the Anishinaabe wants to go into the Midewiwin lodge, everyone speaks only Ojibwe in there. And also when he uses the drums, indeed at that time only the Ojibwe language, the Anishinaabe language, those ones that speak, used it.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa dash ikidowag gichi-Anishinaabeg apiitendaagwak gidinwewininaan Ojibwemowin.
Mii sa geget dash azhigwaa dash giishpin iwapii wii-biindige, wii-piindige Anishinaabe mii keya imaa midewigaaning, eta go Ojibwemowin odaabajitoonaawaan akina awiya biinjayi’iing.
Mii geget sa dash azhigwa aabaji’aajin iniw dewe’iganan, mii sa geget miinawaa dash iwaapii eta go Ojibwemowin, Anishinaabemowin.
wiinawaa gayaagiigidoojig, gaa-aabajitoonaawaa.

paragraph.text_eng: And then as an Indian naming ceremony is going on, certainly the Anishinaabe language is all that they the speakers will use. Indeed, when someone passes, surely the Anishinaabe language is there as well.

sentence.sent_text: Azhigwa dash Anishinaabe-wiinzowin izhi-nibaamagak mii geget sa miinawaa dash Anishinaabemowin mii eta go wii-abajitoonaawaan wiinawaa gayaagiigidojig.
Geget igo azhigwa dash ishkwaanaamod awiya, mii sa geget miinawaa dash Anishinaabemowin ayatemagadoon.

paragraph.text_eng: Yes, that is why today the Ojibwe language, the Anishinaabe language is so important. Indeed the Anishinaabe language will survive here and the Anishinaabe culture. This is what I hope for too, that all the young ones speak Ojibwe.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa geget omaa noongom mii dash omaa ayapiitendaagwak Ojibwemowin, Anishinaabemowin.
Mii sa geget dash omaa apane niigaan da-bimaadizimagak o’o Anishinaabemowin miinawaa dash Anishinaabewin.
O’ow ge-niin bagisendamaan gakina awiya oshki-aya’aag ge-wiinawaa ge waa-netaa-Ojibwemowag.

paragraph.text_eng: They will say it just like those speakers said it long ago. And indeed, the young ones will be able, if they try hard, if they try, indeed they too will properly know our language.

sentence.sent_text: Wii-ikidowag dibishkoo wiinawaa gayaagiigidojig gaa-ikidowaad mewinzha.
Mii geget sa dash ogashkitoonaawaan weshki-aya’aag apane giishpin owiikwajitoonaawaa, giishpin gagwejitoonaawaa o’o geget sa gidinwewininaan weweni sa go ge-wiinawaa ge waa-gikendaanaawaan weweni.

paragraph.text_eng: Indeed the Ojibwe Anishinaabe language is very important. At the time if, if we all try hard, we will be able to save our language, the Ojibwe language. I also hope that the young ones consider this carefully. If their children and grandchildren, if the Ojibwe language is heard, they too, the children today will want to use it. And also later, their grandchildren in the future, they too will know the Anishinaabe language. That is why today this, this is what I think is why the Anishinaabe language, the Ojibwe language is so important.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget ayapiitendaagwak Anishinaabemowin Ojibwemowin.
I’iwaapii dash giishpin, giishpin wiikwajitooyaang gakina, gashkitooyaang da-ishkonamaang gidinwewininaan Ojibwemowin.
Mii ow ge-niin bagosendamaan weweni sa go.

Weshki-aya’aag waa-izhi naanaagadawendamoog o’ow weweni sa go go giishpin, oniijaanisan miinawaa dash oozhisheyan ge-wiinawaa ge-wiin wii-noondaagwak o’ow Ojibwemowin, ge-wiinawaa gaye noongom dash weshki-aya’aag ge-wiinawaa ge owii-aabajitoon o’ow noongom giizhigad.
Miinawaa dash baanimaa apii keyaabi niigaan akeya oozhisheyan wiinawaa ge wii-gikendaanaawaan o’ow Anishinaabe-mowin.
Mii wenji omaa noongom o’ow mii o’ow enendamaan mii wenji omaa apiitendaagwak Anishinaabemowin, Ojibwemowin.

paragraph.text_eng: This is all I want to say at this time. Thanks for listening to me again, that’s it.

sentence.sent_text: mii o’ow waa-ikidoyaan mii zhayiigwa.
Miigwech miinawaa bizindawiyeg mii iw mii iw.

paragraph.text_eng: Indeed I have forgotten a lot; I have forgotten many words. After all I don’t use them everyday anymore when I speak. That is why I forget. This is what is happening now, We’ve almost lost it, our language that was given to us.

sentence.sent_text: Geget igo niibowa niwanendaan iw, niwanendaanan iniw ikidowinan.
Aaniish naa gaawiin endaso-giizhik indaabajitoosiinan geyaabi gaagiidoyaan.
Mii wenji-wanendamaan.
Mii zhigwa ezhiwebak noongom ow.
Gegaa wanitooyang iw, gidinweweninaan gaa-miinigoowiziyang.

paragraph.text_eng: Good Ojibwe speakers, really good speakers are becoming fewer. But there are these new speakers, those that are pursuing Ojibwe. I really like that they are doing it. But there is just one thing that the new speakers do not have. Humor. The Anishinaabe told about all kinds of things when they had a good time, always laughing. The new second-language speaker today doesn’t have that, what is called, what the white man calls “humor.”

sentence.sent_text: Eshkam igo ani-bangiishenhwagizi aw netaa-ojibwemod waanda-ojibwemod.
Ongow dash gaye weshki-ojibwemojig beminizha’angig iw Ojibwemowin.
Geget niminwendaan izhichigewaad iw.
O’ow dash eta gaawiin odayaanziinaawaa ingiw weshki-ojibwemojig iw.
Baapi’idiwin.
Anooj ko gii-inaajimo Anishinaabe gii-minawaanigozid, apane gii-paapid.
Wa’aw noongom, weshki-ojibwemod gaawiin odayaanziin iw, ow izhinikaade, izhinikaadang aw chimookimaan iw “humor.”

paragraph.text_eng: And also today the new Ojibwe speaker is losing the way the Anishinaabe here practiced their spirituality, what he did here. He is losing the way he offered tobacco and had ceremonies. That is all the new speaker is still lacking.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa gaye aw noongom weshki-ojibwemod owanitoon iw akeyaa Anishinaabe gaa-pi-izhitwaaa, gaa-pi-izhiged.
Owanitoon ge iw keyaa izhichiged aw Anishinaabe asemaaked, zagaswe’iwed.
Meta go iw menezid aw geyaabi, weshki-ojibwemod.

paragraph.text_eng: See at our dances over in Mille Lacs and over there, over on the other side of the river (Wisconsin), St. Croix and Lac du Flambeau and over in LCO, the ones that know the dances are becoming fewer.

sentence.sent_text: Ke ge, giniimi’idiwininaan iwidi keyaa Misizaaga’iganing miinawaa oodi, iwidi Agaaming ezhinikaadeg, “St.
Croix” miinawaa imaa “Lac Du Flambeau” miinawaa imaa Odaawaa-zaaga’iganing, bebangiishenhwagiziwag gekendangig iw niimii’idiwii.

paragraph.text_eng: I wish the young speaker would pursue the way we practice our culture, to use what the Spirit gave us to use when we ask them for life.

sentence.sent_text: Begish aw weshki-ojibwemod biminizha’ang iw keyaa ezhitwaayang, da-aabajitooyang iw keyaa Manidoo gaa-miininang da-aabajitooyang gagwejimangwaa iw bimaadiziwin.

paragraph.text_eng: See another thing is at the dance, Ojibwe is always used, and when someone names children, when they give a name, they have to speak good Ojibwe. And also the funeral, when the Anishinaabe is sent off, the person doing it has to speak good Ojibwe. And when a dish is set, and the Anishinaabe sends it up to the Creator, he has to speak Ojibwe. These are what the ones who can speak Ojibwe well do not know yet. Maybe they’ll pursue it later. There are those who do a little of that.

sentence.sent_text: Ke gaye bezhig mii iw niimii’idiwin apane aabijichigaadeg omaa ojibwemowin, miinawaa awiya wiindaawasod, miigiwed iw izhinikaazowin, booch da-nitaa-ojibwemod.
Miinawaa ge iw maajaa’iwewin maajaa’ind aw Anishinaabe, booch da-nitaa-ojibwemod aw ezhichiged.
Miinawaa onaaganan achigaadeg, baa-apagizomind aw Anishinaabe, booch da-ojibwemod.
Mii iniw gekendanzig a’aw netaa-ojibiwemood mashi.
Maagizhaa naagaj oga-biminizha’aan iw Ayaawag wiin go bangii ezhichigejig iw

paragraph.text_eng: It is great that they are pursuing the Ojibwe language; indeed it is great they are speaking Ojibwe for the first time.

sentence.sent_text: Geget onishishin iw biminizha’amowaad ojibwemowin geget onishishin iw oshki-ojibwemowaad.

paragraph.text_eng: There is more that they should know about the use of tobacco. I hope they pursue it.

sentence.sent_text: Baataniinad dash iw nawaj ge-gikendamowaad aw asemaa aabaji’ind.
Pegish biminizha’amowaad i’iw.

paragraph.text_eng: Who will do the speaking in the dance hall? Who is going to speak? Who is going to do naming ceremonies? Who is going to conduct funerals? Who is going to speak for/send the tobacco? I hope they pursue more of that.

sentence.sent_text: Awenen ge-gaagiigidod imaa niimi’idiiwigamigong?
Awenen ge-gaagiigidod?
Awenen ge-izhichiged iw da-wiindaawasod?
Awenen ge-izhichiged iw maajaa iwewin?
Awenen ge-apagizomaad asemaan?
Pegish biminizha’amowaad nawaj iw.

paragraph.text_eng: And some say, more elders, “Don’t write it in a book, don’t!”

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa ge aanind ikidowag ingiw nawaj gechi-aya’aawijig, “Gego ozhibii’angen imaa mazina’iganing gego.”

paragraph.text_eng: What is someone to do to know it if it isn’t written in a book? See today, we live far away. We are being infested by the white man.

sentence.sent_text: Aaniish ge-izhichiged a’aw da-gikendang awiya ozhibii’igaadesinog imaa mazina’iganing?
Nashke noongom, chi-wewaasa gidaamin.
Giningweshkoo giningweshkaagonaan aw chi-mookomaan.

paragraph.text_eng: The Anishinaabe long ago also, when they made their communities, they lived close to one another. Everyone there spoke Ojibwe; everybody listened to it. That is how they came to know things. But today we live far away in different places.

sentence.sent_text: Ge-wiin mewinzha a’aw Anishinaabe, gii-oodenaawichigewaad bebesho gii-taawag.
Kina awiya gii-ojibwemod imaa kina awiya gii-pizindang.
Mii gaa-onji-gikendamowaad wiinawaa gegoo.
Noongom dash, chi-wewaasa bakaan gibaa-daamin.

paragraph.text_eng: There are many different speeches in Ojibwe for when tobacco is sent. I wish the young speaker would pursue more of that.

sentence.sent_text: Baataniinad bakaan gaagiigidowin ojibwemong iw, asemaa apagizomind.
Pegish nawaj biminizha’ang aw weshki-ojibwemod.

paragraph.text_eng: And also in the future, the young Anishinaabe Ojibwe speaker will sound a little different. The new speaker will sound strange. He doesn’t have it, he won’t have what is called the “Indian Accent.”

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa ge bangii niigaan aw Anishinaabe weshki-ojibwemod bakaan da-ni-inwe.
Da-mayagitaagozi aw weshki-ojibwemod.
Gaawiin odayaanziin iw oga-ayaanziin iw “Indian Accent” izhinikaadeg.

paragraph.text_eng: Maybe that’s as much as I want to tell these new Ojibwe speakers, to pursue more of it. The language for when tobacco is being talked for, for speaking.

sentence.sent_text: Mii ganabaj eta minik waa-izhi-wiindamawagwaa ongow weshki-ojibwemojig, da-biminizha’amowaad iw nawaj.
Ojibwemowin apagizomind aw asemaa, da-gaagiigidong.

paragraph.text_eng: That is as much as I want to say before I make someone mad; I don’t want to make anyone mad.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta wiin igo imaa minik waa-ikidoyaan jibwaa-nishkimag awiya, gaawiin niwii-nishkimaasiin awiya.

paragraph.text_eng: Alright thank you, thank you for the tobacco; I shall give thanks for the tobacco first that was given to me because this is our teaching to always use our tobacco; the smoke will go far, far away the tobacco that we use.

sentence.sent_text: Ahaw miigwech, ho miigwech owe asemaa, aaniishinaa akawe inga-miigwechiwendam owe asemaa kaa-shooshkonamaagowaan aaniishinaa mii awe gigikino’amaagoowininaan owe ji-aabaji’ang apane awe gidasemaanaan waasa, waasa da-inaabaso awe asemaa apane gaa-aabaji’ang.

paragraph.text_eng: And then this one, one of the keepers of our language, our Ojibwe language, the American goldfinch is her name; she is bright yellow. She also carries an Indian name just like us we carry our Indian names; we carry our Indian names that we were given. The spirits give us our Indian names that we carry. Wezaawibinesiik is her Indian name is what I was told. I was told in the wigwam when I asked this, “Who should we give tobacco to when we work with the Anishinaabe language, and some may call it Ojibwemowin.” This is one that I was told and that I was pointed to, the American gold finch. This is the one that everyone should offer tobacco to and give food offerings to. Just like how we treat someone when we want to thank them or acknowledge them. This is the American goldfinch as I was told.

sentence.sent_text: Aya’aa dash’a awe bezhig, bezhig awe gaa ganawendang owe gidinwewininaan gidanishinaabemowininaan aginjibagwesi izhinikaazo, ozaawizi aw bineshii.
Wiizo go gaye anishinaabe-wiinzowin ombimiwidoon, mii go dibishkoo gaye giinawind apane gibimiwidoomin gidanishinaabe-wiinzowininaanin gaa-gii-miinininangwaa ogowe.
Adizookaanag gigii-miinigonaanig onowen wiinzowinan gaa-bimiwidooyang.
Wezaawibinesiik izhinikaazo ingii-igonaaban awe.

Ingii-onji-waawiindamaago imaa aya’iing wiigiwaaming gii-kagwedweyaan owe, “awenenda, awenenda awe ge-miinindiban ini asemaan owe gii-dazhiikamang owe anishinaabe-gaagiigidowin, ojibwemowin gemaa ge aanind awiya gii-ikidowag.” Mii dash owe bezhig ga’-wiindamaagowaan gaa-izhinoo’amaagowaan aginjibagwesii.
Mii sa awe bezhig ge-biindaakonegigoban ge-ashamegoban.
Mii sa go gaa-izhi-ind awiya gegoo gii-nanaakomind gii-ayaad gii-miigwechiwi’ind gegoo awiiya mii awe… Mii a’aw aginjibagwesi gaa-inind ingii-igoonaaban.

paragraph.text_eng: And this is the message that I too want to pass on.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash ko awe ezhi-waawiindamaageyaan ge niin.

paragraph.text_eng: So for instance when it is spring and the goldfinches arrive this is what I do at home where I am from. I hang up a bird feed bag and that is how he gets fed this one, the finch. Sometimes I put my leftover meal outside. This is where they come to eat, all of his little relatives, and he has a lot of them, the finch and all the other birds.

sentence.sent_text: Nashke owe gii-siigwang gii-dagoshinowaad ogowe aginjibagwesiiwag mii niin akawe esh-chigeyaan owe idi go bownji-ayaayaan endaayaan.
Indagoodoon owe aya’ii mashkimodens mii dash imaa wendanjiged awe, awe aginjibagwesii.
Ingoding gaye indatoon gegoo ishkonjigan iwidi agwajiing.
Mii go imaa wenji-wiisiniwaad gakina awe odinaawemaaganesa’baatayiinowa’owe aginjibagwesi gaye bineshiinyag.

paragraph.text_eng: As I listen to the ones that know things (the teachers), you should hang tobacco outside. The yellow cloth, just like the way he looks, that goldfinch. This is what you should hang up outside your house, maybe even inside your house. Just as the same color as the finch, this is where you shall tie up the tobacco. This is what I pass on to them, those ones that teach the Indian language. To hang up the tobacco up wherever they teach in their classrooms.The ones that were given the job to pass the language on also our way of life of the things we were told to live a good life.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa awe gaa-izhi-noondawagwaa gekendamowaad gegoo, asemaa, asemaa gidaa-agonaa imaa agwajiing.
Mii dash i’iwe gaa-bagaki-ozaawegak gaa-izhinaagozid sa go awe aginjibagwesii.
Mii awe ge-agoodooyan imaa e’iing agwajiing endaayan, booshke na imaa biindig endaayan.
Mii go ge owe ge-izhinaagwak awe aginjibagwesi gaa-izhinaagozid mii imaa ge-izhi-gashkapinad a asemaa.
Mii dash ko ge owe ezhi-waawiindamawangwaa ogowe, gaa-gikinoo’amaagewaad owe anishinaabemowin, ojibwemowin.
Chi-agoonaawaad asemaan imaa aandi endazhi-gikinoo’amaagewaad inowe gikinoo’amaadiwigamigoon.
Gaa-miinindwaa owe anokiiwin ji-aazhawinamaagewaad owe anishinaabe gaagiigidowin owe Sago gaye gidinaadiziwininaan gaa-izhiwiindamaagooyang gegoo ge-izhi-mino-bimaadiziyang.

paragraph.text_eng: This is the one that always listens and hears how we speak and that is why he needs to be offered tobacco so we can show that we are carrying on our traditions and to carry on the things we were told to do. So we can think kindly/honoring her, the yellow female bird the goldfinch.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dog awe bezhig apane bezandawinang mii dash imaa ezhi-andawendang chi-miinind ono asemaan mii sa go ji inaakidooyang owe gaa-izhi-gikinoo’maagooyang gaa-izhi-wiindamaagooyang ge izhichigeyang.
Weweni ji-naanaagadawenimang awe, wezaawibinesiik aginjibagwesi enind.

paragraph.text_eng: This is one of the things that they (the teachers)I hope they would honor. There are many of them that work on this, who are passing on the knowledge of the Anishinaabemowin also Ojibwemowin. This is my wish that they will carry on.

sentence.sent_text: Mii iwe miinawaa bezhig ambegish gewiinawaa gikendamowaad ogowe.
Baatayiinowag gaa-dazhiikamowaad owe, wii-kagwe-aazhawinimaagewaad owe Anishinaabe gaagiigidowin ojibwemowin gemaa ge.
Mii iw miinawaa bezhig ambegish gewiinawaa izhichigewaad ogowe.

paragraph.text_eng: These ones that are teaching I also want to add on a little bit more. I too taught the native language and worked on it for over twenty years. First I asked elders. First I asked around; I asked the native people, the elders, “How should I do this?” I asked them. And this one told me; it was an elder lady that told me this.

sentence.sent_text: Ogowe gaa-gikinoo amaagewaad bangiichiwiinigo geyaabi imaa inga-ani-bakwebidoon gegoo.
Mewinzha geniin ingii-pi-gikinoo’amaage owe Anishinaabemowin gabe-ii ingii-tazhiikaan awashime niishtana daso-biboon.
Akawe dash ingii-babaa-gagwejimaag Anishinaabeg gichi-aya’aag “Aniin da naa ge-izhichigeyaan gwek?” ingii-anaag.
Mii dash awe bezhig gaa-izhid awe, mindimooyehn awe gaa-gii-izhid.

paragraph.text_eng: She said you should always use your spirit name and honor it with tobacco, the name that was given to you to carry you through. Also to show (the spirit)who you are as a woman, and to always wear your dress.

sentence.sent_text: Apane gidaa-minjimendaan iwe giwiinzowin apane gidaa-aabajitoon iwe giwiinzowin gidaa-biindaakoodoon gaye, owe gaa-miinigoowiziyan ji-bimiwidooyan wiinzowin.
Miinawaa dash owe chi-naakidooyan awenen ayaawiiyan ezhi-ikwewiyan apane ji-gigishkaman iwe magoodaas.

paragraph.text_eng: This is what I was told, and I say this just for (whatever). This is what they told me. I am not trying to change anybody else’s ways maybe their teachings are different from mine. We all have our own teachings as we were growing up. So this is all, thank you.

sentence.sent_text: Mii iwe miinawaa gaa-izhi-waawiindamaagowaan anishaa wiin igo owe indibaajim, Aaniishinaa niin iwe ingii-wiindamaago.
Gaawinoon awiiya gegoo ingagwe-gagaanimaasii bakaan gewiin, bagaan gewiin awiiya gii-izhi-wiindamawaadagenag anishinaa gakina.
Gakina gidayaamin onowe gaa-tibaajimotaagooyang gii-pi-ombigiyang, Wa’mii sa go naa iw.
miigwech.

chapter.eng_title: Why the Anishinaabe Way of Life is Valued

paragraph.text_eng: Greetings, my name is Ozaawaagosh. I am from this reservation Lac du Flambeau. I was given tobacco from my friend, and at this time they asked me; why the Indian way of life is so highly valued? For certain, befor e the white race arrived, our Anishinaabe life and culture was here, at the time it came to be written there in the treaty.

sentence.sent_text: Boozhoo, Ozaawaagosh nindizhinikaaz.
O’o omaa Waaswaagan-ishkoniganiing nindoonjibaa geniin, Asemaa ingii-pi-miinig niijkiiwehns, i’iwapii dash ingii-gagwejimig; aaniish wenji-apiitendaagwak Anishinaabe-bimaadiziwin?
Geget Anishinaabe-bimaadiziwin, i’iwapii dash gii-pi-dagoshinoog i’iwapii ozhibii’igaadeg mii keyaa imaa chi-mazinaa’iganiing.

paragraph.text_eng: So now, this is why I want to speak a little bit here today, for I shall firstly talk carefully about what I too remember of what happened, what had happened in the past while the ancestors lived their lives here in this land of the Anishinaabe People.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash omaa noongom, mii wenji omaa niwii-ikid bebangii omaa, noongom dash inga-dazhindaan akawe dash omaa noongom weweni sa go mikwendamaan geniin gaa-izhiwebak, gaa-izhiwebak ishkweyaang azhigwa gete-Anishinaabe gaa-izhi-bimaadiziwaad o’o omaa Anishinaabewaakiing.

paragraph.text_eng: Certainly those ancestors were adept. At that time they were able to live their lives carefully, surely they were wise; they were adept Anishinaabe people. At that time those Anishinaabe were almost never hungry. They went to various places searching around for food. At that time they were able to receive the spiritual gift of wild animals, fish, and birds. And it is certain the ancestors were very knowledgeable at that time.

sentence.sent_text: Geget igo wewaawiingeziiwag agiw gichi-Anishinaabeg.
I’iwapii dash gaskitoonaawaa da-bimaadiziwaad weweni, mii geget sa wiinawaa gekendaasojig wiinawaa waawiingeziiwag.
Anishinaabeg i’iwapii gegaa gaawiin wiikaa gii-bakadesiiwag.
Agiw Anishinaabeg anooj ingoji gii-izhaawaad azhigwa bebaa-nandawenjigewaad i’iwapii gashkitoonaawaa odaapinamowaad manido-miinigowin awesiiyag, miinawaa giigoonyag, miinawaa bineshiinyag.
Mii geget sa miinawaa gete-aya’aag niibowa ogii-gikendaanaawaan i’iwapii.

paragraph.text_eng: And so when I was a boy here, I listened intently to them, the speakers, and the wise-ones here in Lac du Flambeau. And I listened to the various things said by those speakers. That is why here today I have come to know things and also, I too do not know how to carefully speak the Ojibwe language. It is only a little bit of the Ojibwe language that I speak.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash omaa noongom azhigwa geniin gwiiwizensiwiyaan, bebizindawagwaa wiinawaa, gayaagiigidojig, miinawaa wiinawaa gekendaasojig o’o omaa Waaswaaganiing.
Miinawaa dash azhigwa bizindawagwaa agiw gayaagiigidojig anooj gegoo wiinawaa gaa-ikidowaad.
Mii wenji omaa noongom mii o’o de-bi-gikendamaan miinawaa dash, omaa noongom geniin gaawiin weweni nenitaa-Ojibwemosiin.
Mii eta go bangii Ojibwemoyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: I do not know everything; I only know a little bit. For I too am pitiable, as I properly try to talk today about what happened there in the past.

sentence.sent_text: Gaawiin gakina gegoo ningikendanziin, mii eta go bangii ningikendaan.
Mii dash geniin goopadiziyaan azhigwa noongom dash weweni sa gO awe gojitooyaan omaa da-dazhindaan gaa-izhiwebad mii keyaa imaa ishkweyaang.

paragraph.text_eng: This is only some of what I will repeat, the same as what the speakers and wise-ones said. Surely it is sometimes difficult here while they lived long ago. The ancestor almost had nothing, only the bow. They had that and thus they had hardly anyone else. It is certain that the ancestor was able to shoot the deer with arrows, and then in time the ancestor shot the deer with a gun, and thus he did not go hungry. That is why still to this day the deer are highly valued.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go naabinootaageyaan aanind, dibishkoo wiinawaa gayaagiigidojig wiinawaa gekendasojig gaa-ikidowaad.
Mii sa geget omaa zanagak naanigidinong azhigwa gaa-izhi-bimaadiziwaad mewinzha.
Gegaa gawiin gegoo ogii-ayaanziinaawaa gichi-Anishinaabe, mii eta go mitigwaab.
Ogii-ayaawaa miinawaa dash gegaa gawiin awiiya ogii-ayaawaasiin.

Mii sa geget dash gaashkitood a’aw gichi-Anishinaabe gaa-izhi-bimwaa waawaashkeshi, i’iwapii dash miinawaa waawaashkeshiwan gii-baaskizwaan a’aw gichi-Anishinaabe gaawiin dash bakadesiin mii wenji geyaabi dash dibishkoo noongom geyaabi apiitendaagoziwag waawaashkeshiyag.

paragraph.text_eng: So sometimes the ancestor got in his canoe and there on the lake he went. The ancestor, he went to various places when he harvested wild rice and when he fished, and thus that ancestor did not go hungry.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa naaningodinong ogii-boozi’imaa ojiimaan miinawaa dash mii keyaa imaa zaaga’iganing gii-izhaad gete-aya’aa.
Gete-Anishinaabe, anooji ingoji gii-izhaad azhigwa dash gii-manoominiked miinawaa dash gii-giigooniked, miinawaa dash i’iwapii miinawaa gaawiin bakadesii a’aw gete-Anishinaabe.

paragraph.text_eng: And so here today I am talking about what has happened at that time in our past, of the multitude of things that they, the ancestors, did. And here now while I talk about what has happened in our past, I still remember what happened when I was a boy here on this Lac du Flambeau reservation.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa dash omaa noongom azhigwa dazhindaan gaa-izhiwebad i’iwapii ishkweyaang neniibowa gaa-izhichigewaad wiinawaa gichi-Anishinaabeg.
Mii geget sa omaa noongom azhigwa dazhindaan gaa-izhiwebad ishkweyaang geyaabi dash mikwenimaan gaa-izhiwebad azhigwa geniin gwiiwizenswiyaan o’o omaa Waaswaagan-ishkoniganing.

paragraph.text_eng: We were an impoverished Anishinaabe people here on the Lac du Flambeau reservation. At that time my only home was a shack with my father and mother. My father; at this time it is difficult talking about my parents.

sentence.sent_text: Chi-gidimaagoziyaang Anishinaabeg o’o omaa Waaswaagan-ishkoniganing.
I’iwapii eta go waakaa’iganish endayaan miinawaa dash nibabaayiban miinawaa nimamaayiban, Nindedeyiban; i’iwapii zanagak azhigwa nindazhimaag nigitiziimag.

paragraph.text_eng: My mother’s name is Inaate’biig, carefully they did various things while I was a boy. At that time commodity foods had not yet arrived. If they were hungry at that time, the Anishinaabe people went out hunting for food. That is what happened when I too was a boy.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa nimamaayiban Inaate’biig izhinikaazo weweni sa go anooj gegoo gaa-izhichigewaad azhigwa gwiiwizenswiyaan.
I’iwapii dash gaawiin mashi dagoshinziimagak i’iw ashandiwin izhi-wiindemagak.
Giishpin bakadewag i’ iwapii, Anishinaabeg waa-izhi-nandawejigewag.
Mii gaa-izhiwebad azhigwa geniin gwiiwizenswiyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: While I was a boy I first recall this one time when it was halfway through the winter and we were snowshoeing on a beaver lodge. We were trapping, as we arrived those things [tools] were there. At that time my father always trapped those beaver, that’s what my father did at that time. And he also did various things during winter, and so subsequently he caught walleye. And sometimes my father crawled inside, inside there, the little spearing house. While he speared through the ice, he jigged [with a stick] as he used that wooden decoy fish. Thus at that time he lured those pike and then he was able to spear them. And at that time we surely did not go hungry, for my father knew the proper way of things.

sentence.sent_text: Azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan ingoding akawe o’o mikwendamaan i’iwapii aabita-biboon mii dash ingii-aagimosemin amikwiishsan.
E-atemagadoon azhigwa dash ingii-dagoshiniminin imaa ingii-wanii’igemin i’iwapii.
I’iwapii dash nindedeyiban apane ogii-dasoonaawaan aniw amikwan.
Mii gaa-izhichiged i’iwapii indede, mii miinawaa dash anooj gaa-izhichiged nibaabaayiban azhigwa biboon miinawaa dash ogaawan oo ogii-debibinaan.
Miinawaa dash naaningodinong wii-biindoode mii keyaa imaa biinjay’ii imaa akwawaa-wigamigoons azhigwa dash gaa-izhi-akwawaad nibaabaayiban.

Gii-chiichiibinaabi azhigwa dash aabajitood i’iw mitigo-giigoozenhs i’iwapii dash gaa-izhi-wayezhimaad iniw ginoozhewan mii dash gashkitood da-bazhibowaan mii geget sa i’iwapii gaawiin dash ingii-bakadesiimin azhigwa dash weweni sa go anooj gegoo ogii-gikendaan nibaabaayiban.

paragraph.text_eng: Sometimes during the winter when he went to the swamp he used a snare, as it is called. After the snares are hung, that is when he got rabbits. And so while the snares hung on the rabbit trail, that is the time we did not go hungry for my father was skillful. This is what he did in the winter.

sentence.sent_text: Naaningodinong dash azhigwa biboon mii keyaa imaa waabishkikiing gii-izhaad nagwaagan, ezhiwiindemagak gii-aabajitood.
Azhigwa dash geget sa ishkwag dash agoodemagak, mii apii dash aniw waaboozoon ogii-debibinaan.
Azhigwa dash agoodemagakinoon nagwaaganan mii ke imaa waaboozo-miikanensiing miinawaa dash, i’iwapii gaawiin ingii-bakadesiimin azhigwa gii-nitaawiged nibaabaayiban.
Mii gaa-izhichiged azhigwa biboong.

paragraph.text_eng: And so then it was the time when we went there in the woods while the sap began to flow in the sugarbush. Surely, the Anishinaabe did many things. This is when I recall those maple trees, as they are called, standing there in the woods, there in the sugarbush. Certainly it is highly valued, that which they did while the Anishinaabe people made sugar. At this time the Anishinaabe always worked very hard. This is what I remember they did when I was a boy.

sentence.sent_text: I’iwapii dash miinawaa mii keyaa imaa mitigoogwaakiing ingii-izhaamin azhigwa dash geget sa onjigaamagak mii keyaa imaa iskigamiziganing.
Mii geget sa, anooj gegoo Anishinaabeg gaa-izhichigewaad.
I’iwapii weweni sa go mikwenimaan mii geget sa idash iniw ininaatigoog, izhinikaazowag, wiinawaa gaabawiwag mii keyaa imaa mitigoogwaakiing, mii keyaa imaa iskigamiziganing.
Mii geget sa apiitendaagwak gaa-izhichigewaad azhigwa dash Anishinaabeg gii-ozhitoonaawaa Anshinaabe-ziinzibaakwad.
I’iwapii gichi-anokiiwag pane Anishinaabeg.
I’iwapii mii o mikwenimaan gaa-izhichigewag azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: And thus, in the direction there, in the direction there by the lake and river, we went while the Anishinaabe speared fish by torchlight. As they harvested fish, over there, they used a spear while spearing walleye and muskies, as they are called. And certainly at this time we did not go hungry.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa dash, mii keyaa imaa, miinawaa dash mii keyaa imaa zaaga’iganing miinawaa ziibing, ingii-izhaamin azhigwa dash Anishinaabe gii-waaswaaganikewaad.
Azhigwa giigoonikewaad azhigwa owidi anitiin gii-aabajitoonaawaa azhigwa dash ogii-bazhinbawan iniw giigooyag ogaawag miinawaa maashkinoozheyag izhinikaazowag.
Geget igo i’iwapii miinawaa gaawiin ingii-bakadesiimin.

paragraph.text_eng: And thereafter, we went to various places picking berries. Firstly, were the strawberries as it is named, and then the blueberries are picked. And so at this time we did not go hungry.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa dash, azhigwa dash miinawaa anooj ingoji ingii-izhaamin azhigwa dash ingii-mawinzomin.
Akawe idash ode’iminan ezhiwiindemagak, wiinawaa miinan odaapinigaadeg.
Miinawaa dash i’iwapii gaawiin ingii-bakadesiimin.

paragraph.text_eng: And we did various things in the summer; this is when the firefly arrived.’This is the time when we begin to hunt. Yes, this is the time when my father shot deer. This is what happens when that firefly, that insect, arrives this way. And so at this time we did not go hungry.

sentence.sent_text: Anooj dash azhigwa niibing anooj gegoo ingii-izhichigemin azhigwa dash mii gii-pi-dagoshing gii-pi-dagoshing na’aw waawaatesii.

Mii sa geget, i’iwapii dash miinawaa maajii-giiyosemin eya’i’iwapii dash waawaashkeshiwan nimbaabaa gii-baashkizwaan mii gaa-izhiwebak azhigwa dash gii-bi-dagoshin miinawaa dash a aw waawaatesii a’aw manidoons i iwapii dash miinawaa gaawiin weweni ingii-bakadesiimin.

paragraph.text_eng: When my father killed those deer, he used practically everything when he was able to, the buckskin, and all the flesh, and alsothe brains when my father tanned hides. Surely, this is why here today the deer is still highly valued, For certain, I too respect that deer.

sentence.sent_text: Gegaa gakina gegoo ogii-aabajitood azhigwa dash gashkitood nibaabaayiban megwaa ogii-nisaan iniw waawaashkeshiwan, waawaashkeshiwayaan miinawaa dash gakina wiiyaas miinawaa dash owiinimdib gii-aseked miinawaa dash nibaabaayinban.
Geget sa mii onji idash omaa noongom geyaabi apiitendaagozi waawaashkeshi geget igo geniin nindapiitenimawaa a’aw waawaashkeshi geniin.

paragraph.text_eng: And definitely, at this time in our lives, during the Ricing Moon, we went there to the rice beds, for there were various things we did. As we arrived there at the wild rice beds, when we harvested wild rice, all of my various tools were already there; the knocking sticks, the push pole, and the canoe. When we harvested wild rice there on the rice beds, at this time when the Anishinaabe-rice was picked, we definitely did not go hungry. And still today, this Anishinaabe-rice is highly valued.

sentence.sent_text: Geget sa, i’iwapii dash azhigwa bimaadiziyaang, mii keyaa dash azhigwa Manoominke-giizis, miinawaa dash ingii-izhaamin mii keyaa imaa manoominkaang, geget sa dash anooj gegoo ingii-izhichigemin.

Azhigwa dash ingii-dagoshinimin mii keyaa imaa manoominikaang miinawaa dash bawaa’iganaatigoon miinawaa dash gaandaki’iganaatig miinawaa dash jiimaan mii miinawaa dash anooj gegoo nindaabajichiganan etemagadoon azhigwa dash ingii-manoominkemin mii keyaa imaa manoominikaang geget sa dash i’iwapii miinawaa gaawiin bakadesiimin azhigwa dash Anishinaabe manoomin odaapinigaadeg.
Miinawaa dash noongom geyaabi apiitendaagwak i’iw Anishinaabe-manoomin.

paragraph.text_eng: And so then as it got colder in the time of the Falling Leaves Moon, we went there to the water as we were trapping. For sure it is the muskrat my father trapped. And thereafter I ate muskrat, and we lived at that time not going hungry.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa dash azhigwa nawaj gisinaa i’iwapii Binaakwe-giizis, mii miinawaa dash mii keyaa imaa nibiikaang ingii-ayaamin azhigwa dash ingii-wanii’igemin.
Geget sa wazhashkwag nimbaabaa ogii-odasoonaan iniw wazhashkwan mii miinawaa dash ingii-amwaag wazhashkwag, azhigwa dash bimaadiziyang i’iwapii miinawaa gaawiin ingii-bakadesiimin.

paragraph.text_eng: Certainly there were all kinds of things we did while living the proper Anishinaabe way of life when I was a boy. And certainly there was always a lot of hard work while we lived at that time.

sentence.sent_text: Geget igo akina gegoo anooj gegoo ingii-izhichigemin azhigwa ingii-bimaadizimin weweni sa go Anishinaabewin izhi-bimaamagak i’iwapii azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan.
Geget igo apane, apane chi-anokiiwin azhigwa dash bimaadiziyang i’iwapii.

paragraph.text_eng: It is quite different nowadays for almost all the food today is elsewhere; certainly it is there at the store. When the Anishinaabe, the young Anishinaabe wants to go out if they are hungry, it is over there to the store they now go.

sentence.sent_text: Bakaan igo noongom dash gegaa gakina ingoji noongom dash wiisiniwin atemagadoon noongom geget sa mii keya imaa adaawewigamigong.
Anishinaabe, oshki-Anishinaabe wii-izhaawag noongom dash giishpin bakade giishpin bakadewag mii keya imaa adaawewigamigong izhaawag noongom i’iwapii.

paragraph.text_eng: We were not able to go there to the store; we were poor Anishinaabe, almost in tatters. At that time we did not have money; we were poor, and so we were not able to go to the store to make purchases at that time. That is why we always went there to the lake and forest when I was a boy.

sentence.sent_text: Gaawiin dash gashkitoosiimin da-izhaad mii keyaa imaa adaawewigamigong sidimaagoziyaang gegaa, gegaa bagoshkaamagak Anishinaabe.
I’iwapii dash gaawiin zhooniyaa ingii-ayaawaasiimin i’iwapii dash gidimaagoziyaang gaawiin dash mii keyaa imaa adaawewigamigong gaawiin ingashktoosiimin gegoo da adaawe i’iwaapii.
Mii dash mii wenji pane mii keyaa imaa zaaga’iganing miinawaa mitigoowaakiing ingii-izhaamin azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: Not until that commodity food, as it is called, when the white man gave the Anishinaabe food that was inside there, the cans; at this time is when a lot of diabetes came, after the commodities arrived there in Anishinaabe country. Certainly the food was different, and so this is not the proper Anishinaabe way of life.

sentence.sent_text: Baanimaa apii dash a’aw ashanidiwin izhiwiindemagak, mii apii dash aw chimookomaan i’iwapii dash ogii-miinaan Anishinaabe miijim ategin imaa biinjayi’iing imaa akikoons akikoonsag geget sa bakaan wiisiniwin atemagak gaawiin dash weweni sa go Anishinaabe gaa-izhi-bimaadizisiin i iwapii mii dash iiwapii onzaam ziinzibaakwad-waapinewin ezhi-wiindemagak mii keyaa odaapinigaadeg dash ishkwaa dash ashanidiwin gii-pi-dagoshin imaa Anishinaabewaakiing.

paragraph.text_eng: And certainly here today, I too still try to eat just like the ancestors ate, how they ate in this Anishinaabe way. And so today I am certainly doing well, for I eat that Anishinaabe food received, it is just like medicine. Also when I spear fish, and when shoot the different game animals, it is the same as medicine. And for sure that Anishinaabe rice as well, this is also Anishinaabe medicine. Here in the ceded territory, here in the land of the Anishinaabe and in the water, that medicine is still used.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa omaa noongom, keyaabi geniin wii-kwajitooyaan imaa da-wiisiniyaan dibishkoo gete-aya’aag gaa-wiisiniwaad, gaa-inanjigewaad mii o Anishinaabewin.
Geget sa dash geniin noongom nimino-ayaa, geget sa mii onji omaa dibishkoo mashkiki i’iw wiisiniwin Anishinaabe odaapinigaadeg.
Azhigwa dash nimbazhiba’waan giigoonyag miinawaa dash azhigwa baashkizwaan anooj awesiiyag, dibishkoo mashkikiwan.
Geget igo i’iw Anishinaabe manoomin gaye mii miinawaa gaye dash Anishinaabe mashkiki.
Etemagak omaa Anishinaabewaakiing, omaa Anishinaabewaakiing miinawaa dash nibiikaang, keyaabi dash aabajichigaadeg i’iw Anishinaabe mashkiki.

paragraph.text_eng: And in this, I too am still in good health today, as well as my children. For it is here today while I give this talk here as to what has happened when I was a boy, a young man. And at this time I am a man, a middle-aged man, for certain here today as I talk about how we lived here. It is right while I talk about this. The young ones want to know more, to be able to have a good life as the ancestors did things, and the Anishinaabe way of life will still go on into the future.

sentence.sent_text: Mii o’o’ geniin miinawaa dash keyaabi nimino-ayaa noongom miinawaa ninijaanisag.
Mii dash omaa noongom azhigwa gaagiigidoyaan imaa gaa-izhiwebad azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan miinawaa dash azhigwa a’aw oshki-inini, oshki-inini geniin.
I’iwapii mii miinawaa dash inini miinawaa akiwenzii’enhs noongom dash omaa aawiyaan, mii geget sa omaa noongom azhigwa dazhindaan gaa-izhi-bimaadiziyaang omaa.
Mii geget sa azhigwa dazhindaan o’o.

Nawaj owii-gikendaanaawaan awe weshke’aya’aag dash ge gegiinawaa ge gashkitoonaawaad da-mino-bimaadiziwaad geget sa dibishkoo wiinawaa gete-aya’aag gaa-doodamowaad keyaabi dash niigaan-bimaadizimagak Anishinaabewin.

paragraph.text_eng: And here today, as I properly talk about the way in which they lived long ago, I too saw my parents do the same when I was a boy. And there is more I want to say here today. So I think about this very carefully as to what is going to happen to the people here in Lac du Flambeau, and they will also properly know the Anishinaabe way Of life, for it is very important all of the time.

sentence.sent_text: Mii o’o’ omaa noongom azhigwa weweni sa go dazhidaan gaa-izhi-bimaadiziwaad mewinzha mii miinawaa dash geniin ingii-waabandaan dibishkoo ingitiziimag gaa-izhichigewaad azhigwa azhigwa gwiiwizensiwiyaan.
Mii dash omaa noongom omaa nawaj niwii-ikid azhigwa dash omaa noongom.

Weweni Sa go naanaagadawendamaan weweni sa go waa-izhiwebak niigaan keyaa dash Anishinaabe, Anishinaabe o’o’ omaa Waaswaaganiing dash weweni sa go ge wiinawaa ge-gikendanaawaa o’o Anishinaabewin apiitendaagwak pane.

paragraph.text_eng: Indeed, today only as I speak, I also think that here within the reservation of Lac du Flambeau, everything we did as I went about hunting for food, that everything we did hunting for food was here within the reservation. Indeed at that time something happened. At that time the decision-makers, the judges and our chiefs, decided something that the light-skinned race had remembered; what had happened as our past chiefs had decided long ago, and that which was written in the treaty as it is called.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa mii eta go dash omaa noongom azhigwa gaagiigidoyaan imaa geniin omaa mii o’o’ nindinendam o’o omaa biinjayi’ii omaa ishkoniganiing, Waaswaaganiing gakina gegoo ningii-izhichigemin azhigwa ingii-nandawenjige, ningii-nandawenjigemin omaa biinjayaa omaa ishkoniganiing.
Geget sa dash i’iwapii dash gegoo gaa-izhiwebad.

Mii dash i’iwapii dash wiinawaa dibaakonigejig miinawaa gidoogimaaninaanig gegoo dash gaa-inaakonigewaad dah i’iwapii wayaabishkiiwejig ogii-mikwendaanaawaa izhiwebad azhigwa dash gidoogimaabaniig gaa-inaakoniged gegoo dash mewinzha mii o’pii dash gaa-ozhibii’igaadeg mii keyaa omaa chi-mazina’iganing ezhiwiindemagak.

paragraph.text_eng: Therefore, at that time our past chiefs had decided that still, and always, the Anishinaabe people should be able to go all around the Anishinaabe territory to feed themselves. That was decided long ago. It was the light-skinned race that decided the Anishinaabe couldndeer, he used practically everyth;t go around to feed themselves; this is what the light-skinned race decided. So at that time the game wardens, as they are called, they would arrest the Anishinaabe if he went outside of the reservation to feed himself, and then into the jail he went.

sentence.sent_text: I’iwapii dash gidoogimaaminaabaniig mii o’o gaa-inaakoniged keyaabi dash apane gashkitood Anishinaabeg da-bebaa-aaya’aad omaa Anishinaabewaakiing da-nandwenjiged mii o’o gaa-inaakoniged i’iwapii mewinzha.
Mii sa geget dash i’iwapii wayaabishkiiwejig bakaan gegoo dash i’iwapii gegoo dash gaa-inaakonigewaad gaawiin keyaabi Anishinaabe wii-bayaaba-aya’aad da-nandwenjiged.
Mii o’o gaa-inaakonigewaad wiinawaa wayaabishkiiwejig.

I’iwapii dash izhinikaazowag dakonawewininiwag mii geget sa ogii-takonaan Anishinaabe giishpin mii keyaa omaa awasayi’iing omaa ishkoniganiing gii-izhaad da-nandawenjiged mii dash mii keyaa imaa piinjayi’ii gibaakwa’idiing gii-izhaad Anishinaabe.

paragraph.text_eng: So indeed at that time some had forgotten what had been written there in that treaty, and still the Anishinaabe people went to jail if they left the reservation. So here at that time afterwards, they had decided, once again, the Anishinaabe could feed himself outside the reservation. The Anishinaabe went to various places as he speared walleye, shot deer, made rice outside of the reservation, just like we are still doing today.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa geget dash aanind gaawiin ogii-wanendanziinaawaan gaa-ozhibii’igaadeg mii keyaa imaa chi-mazina’iganiing miinawaa dash keyaabi mii ke imaa gibaakwa’diing gii-izhaad, gii-izhaawaad Anishinaabeg giishpin mii keyaa imaa awasayi’iing ishkoniganiing gii-izhaawaad.
I’iwapii dash ishkwaa dash gaa-inaakonigewaad miinawaa gashkitood Anishinaabe da-izhaad imaa da-nandawenjiged imaa awasayi’iing.

I’iwapii dash miinawa anooj ingoji Anishinaabeg gaa-izhaawaad gii-bazhiba’waan ogaawan miinawaa gii-baashkizwaan waawaashkeshiwan mii miinawaa dash gii-manominikewaad awasayi’iing i’iwapii mii dash noongom dash omaa keyaabi, keyaabi azhigwa o’o doodamaang.

paragraph.text_eng: Still I thank those elders for what they had decided. For at that time they thought about those who would live. And today as I thank them carefully, indeed I wish for this; that the young people here will still remember those elders, and the difficult lives they had as they lived.

sentence.sent_text: Keyaabi nimiigwechiwi’aag wiinawaa gichi-aya’aag dash gaa-inaakonigewaad.
Azhigwa dash ogii-inenamowaad wiinawaa waa-bimaadiziwaad.

Mii geget sa omaa noongom dash azhigwa miigwechiwi’aag weweni sa go dash omaa o’o bagosendamaan oshki-Anishinaabe omaa weweni sa go keyaabi gewiinawaa ge-waa-azha-mikwenimawaan aniw gichi-aya’aag azhigwa geget sa zaanagak bimaadiziwin ogii-ayaanaawaan azhigwa mewinzha gaa-izhi-bimaadiziwaad.

paragraph.text_eng: It is for certain they always made tobacco offerings for things that were received. So indeed here today, the Anishinaabe way of life is still highly important. And so if our young people are to obtain something, beforehand they must make a tobacco offering correctly. This is what the elders were saying. Today I too, whatever it is that I am doing, first I will definitely use tobacco. Indeed here, that is the Anishinaabe way. However, the Americans do not understand this. So indeed if you are Anishinaabe, you too will do this first and foremost, for sure this is highly important; thig Anishinaabe way of life.

sentence.sent_text: Mii geget sa i’iwapii dash pane weweni sa go ogii-biindaakoojigewaad gii-asemaakewaad azhigwa dash gegoo odaapinigaadeg.
Mii sa geget dash omaa noongom apiitendaagwak o’o Anishinaabewin.
Mii miinawaa dash giishpin gashkitoonaawaa noongom dash wiinawaa weshki-aya’aag gegoo gii-odaapinang geget sa dibwaa dash wii-asemaakewaad weweni.
Mii o’o pane gaa-ikidowaad wiinawaa gichi-aya’aag.
Mii dash omaa noongom geniin azhigwa gegoo izhichigeyaan geget sa akawe asemaa nindaabaji’aa.
Mii sa geget imaa Anishinaabewin.

Mii sa geget omaa gaawiin dash wiinawaa chi-mookomaanag gikendanziinaawaan o’o, Geget sa dash giishpin Anishinaabe’aawiyan geget sa gegiin mii o’o kawe gegiin giwii-izhichige mii sa geget omaa noongom geget sa omaa apiitendaagwak o’o Anishinaabe-bimaadiziwin.

paragraph.text_eng: If today we lose what they did long ago, our way of living the Anishinaabe way of life will no longer be here in the future. This is the reason why now, those knowledgeable ones always say, “Don’t forget this way of living.” The Anishinaabe way of life is very important, and the Anishinaabe way of life still continues to live on. If we do just like our ancestors did long ago, for we cannot change how they lived and we are unable to change this, indeed today things are different; however, if the Anishinaabe people use tobacco just as the forbearers did, the Anishinaabe life will be here for us and also, all these things.

sentence.sent_text: Geget sa giishpin dash omaa noongom giishpin ni-wanedanziimin gaa-izhichigewaad mewinzha gaawiin geget sa Anishinaabewin, Anishinaabewin izhiwebasinoon mii keyaa omaa niigaan keyaa.

Geget dash mii wenji omaa noongom dash o’o wiinawaa gekendaasojig pane gaa-ikidowaad, “Gego wanendangen o’o Anishinaabewin.” Anishinaabewin apiitendaagwak miinawa Anishinaabewin keyaabi da-bimaadizimagak niigaan keyaa giishpin keyaabi.

Geget sa giishpin doodamang dibishkoo wiinawaa gete-aya aag gaa-doodamowaad mewinzha gaawiin dash nigashkitoosiimin da-aanjiishkaatoon o’o geget sa noongom dash anooj gegoo bakaan igo noongom; geget sa pane giishpin aabaji’aa asemaan Anishinaabeg geget sa dash dibishkoo wiinawaa gete-aya aag gaa-doodamowaad mii ezhiwebak azhigwa Anishinaabeg, Anishinaabeg bimaadiziwin izhiwebak omaa mii miinawaa dash akina, akina gegoo.

paragraph.text_eng: If today they, the young people at this time, if, he goes somewhere to hunt for food, the Anishinaabe will always value the four-legged ones, all the birds, the little birds, and all that which the spirit has given. It is here now, the young people, myself included, this is what I am wishing for; that they will never forget this, everything is important.

sentence.sent_text: Giishpin noongom wiinawaa weshki-aya’aang i’iwapii dash, giishpin Wii-izhaad ingoji da-nandawenjiged mii sa geget dash weweni sa go apane Anishinaabe waa-izhi apiitenimowaan iniw niiyogaadejig mii minawaa dash akina binesiiyag, miinawaa bineshiiyag, miinawaa dash akina manido-miinigoowin.

Mii sa geget omaa noongom dash miinawaa weshki-aya’aag pane o’o geniin bagosendamaan gaawiin dash niigaan gaawiin dash wiikaa niigaan keyaa wiinawaa waa-izhi-wanedanziinaawaa o’o apiitendaagwak akina gegoo.

paragraph.text_eng: Here today, this is undoubtedly what I think. Our treaty is very important, and also everything in our way of life, the Anishinaabe way of life. Indeed it is just like good medicine, everything we are able to receive, for it is certainly a gift from the Spirit. This is why it is important.
